writing_guide: Every question comes from Procedure 401.4-KC, the Kansas City Medication List by Level (2027 Protocols), approved by the Medical Director in October 2026. If the list and the protocols differ, the protocols govern.
Clinical Education ruling, Oct 2026: opioid and benzodiazepine drips and PCAs are AEMT unless the patient is intubated (sedation alone does not make them Paramedic).
Two answer choices per question, so the wording of a third choice can't give the answer away.
Name drugs the way a nurse says them on the phone: the brand, with the generic in brackets.
Prompts and statements 12 words or fewer; explanations two sentences or fewer.

fluids.name: Fluids & Antibiotics
fluids.tip: Crystalloids, dextrose, potassium on a pump and antibiotics are AEMT. Hypertonic saline, colloids, TPN, blood and antifungals aren't.

comfort.name: Pain, Calm & Comfort
comfort.tip: Opioid and benzo drips and PCAs are AEMT unless the patient is intubated.

als.name: Paramedic Only
als.tip: Pressors, BP and rate drips, heparin, insulin, sedation, Pitocin, Pepcid, Protonix, Keppra, IV Tylenol: Paramedic.

rules.name: Read the Whole List
rules.tip: One drug off the AEMT list, on neither list, or any drip on an intubated patient: Paramedic.
